title: The influence of contexts on expectation effects in pain
summary:
This study investigates expectation effects in pain, so the tendency of negative expectations to worsen pain experiences whereas positive expectations tend to alleviate them. Herein, we try to determine how these expectations may be subjected to environmental influences, i. e. how said expectation effects might change depending on whether you are in a negative versus a positive environment. 
Expectations towards pain will be evoked via a sham brain-computer interface (BCI) which reports brain states of pain susceptibility back to participants. Herein, visual cues with dark or light orange highlighting indicate either a high or a low pain sensitivity. 
This BCI feedback is, unbeknownst to participants, unrelated to actual brain activity and intended to manipulate expectations. The belief in the BCI is evoked through verbal instructions and a conditioning period. In addition to pain and expectation ratings, EEG and electrodermal data will be recorded.

interventions.name: The two conditions (corresponding to Arm 1.1 and 1.2) are presented to each participant in a pseudorandomized order in two virtual environments: (Arm 2.1) in a negative and (Arm 2.2) in a positive environment. Arm 1 and 2 are firstly presented in 3D (Arm 3.1), i. e. on a Virtual Reality headset, and

Arm 2.1 – Negative environment:
A dark, empty subway (https://www.fab.com/listings/39abdcd9-baa1-49a0-bb9b-90808d483bca?lang=en) is supposed to be experienced as more negative. 

Arm 2.2 – Positive environment:
A sunny, empty beach (https://www.fab.com/listings/7d7cc1ab-19f1-4273-a9e6-594105fc2b

Arm 3.1 – 3D:
The experiment is implemented in 3D. The contexts and their respective audios are presented via Oculus Quest 3. 

Arm 3.2 – 2D:
The experiment is implemented on a 2D computer screen with screenshots of the 3D contexts and the respective audio played from computer speakers.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy
Exclusion criteria:
•	Moderate to severe depressive symptoms
•	Presence of acute or chronic somatic, neurological or psychiatric disorders
•	Pregnancy
•	Regular use of medication (except hormonal contraceptives)
•	Use of illegal drugs, regular use of psychotropic or analgesic substances
•	Consumption of caffeine 2 hours before testing and consumption of alcohol on the day of testing and on the previous day
•	Participation in a study involving deception within the past six months
•	Conditions preventing successful EEG measurement (e.g. baldness, skin diseases, etc.)
•	Inclination towards VR-induced nausea or dizziness 
•	Known cases of epilepsy in the immediate family
•	No normal or corrected-to-normal vision
•	After participation, subjects will be excluded from the EEG/SCR analyses when meeting any of the following criteria: (a) if there is no behavioural effect in pain-related expectations (expectation rating placebo condition > nocebo condition) and the placebo pain rating is equal to or higher than the nocebo pain rating, or (b) if EEG/SCR data quality is overly poor, or (c) if the participant expresses explicit disbelief in BCI cover story, or (d) if more than 50% of pain stimuli are rated as non-painful (VAS = 0), or (e) due to insufficient task engagement (not rating within the time limit or not moving the cursor in more than 30% of all trials), or (f) if the intended positive/negative context differences are not rated as such after the experiment
